_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.
_meta.maintenance: Manual updates + Claude WebSearch each session. 2026-08-05 refresh: Japan-US joint intervention confirmed officially by both Treasuries — Bessent said 'we will not hesitate to participate in further joint intervention'; USDJPY trading near 157 as of Aug 5 after hitting 40-year low near 164 pre-intervention. BOJ held at 1% in July but hawkish Ueda signaling a Sept hike, adding fundamental support to intervention. USMCA theme materially upgraded: Section 122 expired Jul 24 and was replaced by Section 301 (10-12.5%); Trump invoked Section 338 on Jul 20 imposing 50% on ~$20B of Canadian goods (autos, dairy, alcohol) effective Aug 19 — USMCA compliance no longer guarantees exemption on those baskets. This is a live binary CAD event with Aug 19 hard deadline. Warsh-Fed theme still structurally intact; July FOMC held with three dissents, 30-yr yield hit 5.21%.

themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — ~$72B+ spent, both Treasuries vow further action, USDJPY ~157
themes.summary: The most significant coordinated G2 FX intervention in over a decade is now confirmed and officially bilateral. Japan MoF had already deployed a record ¥11.73T (~$72.8B) in solo intervention across Apr-May 2026 that ultimately failed, with USDJPY hitting a 40-year low near 164. On Jul 30 Japan struck again in NY trading hours, driving USDJPY down ~3% in a single session. The US Treasury then confirmed direct participation on Jul 31 — the Fed NY sold euros for yen via Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley. Bessent publicly stated 'we will not hesitate to participate in further joint intervention' and endorsed the yen as 'substantially undervalued.' Trump called it 'a signal of friendship' with Japan. As of Aug 5 USDJPY is holding near 157, -4.5% from its pre-intervention high. Key amplifier: BOJ left rates at 1% in July but Governor Ueda struck a 'noticeably more hawkish' tone, with markets pricing a 25bp hike before year-end — this gives fundamental support to the intervention for the first time. ING flags 157 as the re-intervention tripwire. BofA identifies 155 as the psychological flip level where corporate hedgers activate dollar-selling loops. NFP on Aug 7 (consensus: 91K, 4.3% unemployment) is the next binary: a weak print turbocharges intervention; a strong print reignites carry trade mechanics and tests MoF resolve.

implications.JPY: STRONG tailwind — dual-authority intervention with explicit re-entry warning is the most credible yen defence in decades. All JPY-cross SHORTS face active central-bank headwind. BOJ rate-hike expectations provide fundamental multiplier absent in prior intervention episodes.
implications.USD: USDJPY specifically under sustained intervention pressure. Broad DXY also soft given coordinated nature signals US policy preference for weaker dollar vs yen. Other USD pairs less directly impacted but sentiment headwind is real.
implications.EUR: EUR/JPY sold off sharply; note the Fed NY sold euros for yen as the intervention mechanism — EUR bears a mechanical, not just sentiment, role in this episode. EUR/USD testing resistance under unusual distortion.
implications.GBP: GBP/JPY under pressure; indirect spillover into GBP/USD from broader USD softness.
implications.CAD: CADJPY down; CAD dynamics primarily driven by Section 338 tariff theme.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY down; AUD/USD relatively less affected but risk-off tone from intervention volatility is a modest headwind.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY above 157 = ING re-intervention tripwire, expect fresh MoF/Treasury action. USDJPY below 155 = BofA flip level, corporate hedger loops activate, intervention 'winning.' USDJPY back above 160 = market overpowering coordinated defence, theme credibility breaks. Any official MoF/Treasury statement disclaiming further action = theme ends. NFP Aug 7 is the nearest binary catalyst.

themes.title: Warsh Fed hawkish — 5th consecutive hold, three dissents, 30-yr yield at 19-year high 5.21%
themes.summary: July 29 FOMC delivered another hold at 3.5-3.75% — the fifth straight — but with three dissents (hawkish) and a long-end bond market that is clearly not buying the pause narrative. The 30-yr Treasury yield surged 12bps to 5.21% during the post-meeting press conference, its highest in 19 years; the 10-yr rose 7bps to 4.67%. Warsh reiterated commitment to reining inflation and said he views it positively when bond markets react to data rather than Fed signalling. He confirmed elimination of forward guidance is permanent. Median 2026 dot remains at 3.8% (raised from 3.4% at June meeting), with 9 of 18 members projecting at least one hike. Markets have fully priced out any 2026 cuts and now assign meaningful probability to a Dec hike. USD carry trade is structurally intact versus every G10 central bank currently cutting or on hold with easing bias (ECB, BoE, RBA, RBNZ, SNB). The only offsetting force is the Japan intervention theme pushing USDJPY lower against the rate differential.

implications.USD: STRUCTURAL tailwind — hawkish Warsh + hike-tilted dots + 5.21% 30-yr yield = USD carry strongly defended. Exception: USDJPY overridden by active intervention theme.
implications.JPY: STRUCTURAL headwind from rate differential BUT currently overridden by intervention — do not trade USDJPY on this thesis alone.
implications.EUR: headwind — ECB cutting while Fed holds hawkish widens rate differential vs EUR. EUR/USD testing major resistance.
implications.GBP: headwind — BoE cutting; USD carry differential works against GBP.
implications.CAD: mixed — USD structural bid offsets any oil/commodity support; USDCAD structurally biased up, compounded by Section 338 tariff pressure.
implications.AUD: headwind — RBA on hold with easing bias; carry disadvantaged vs USD.
implications.CHF: headwind — SNB in easing mode; USDCHF supported.

themes.watchLevel: Any Warsh softening in speeches or hint of cuts re-entering the dot plot = pivot back in play, unwinds theme. Sub-3.0% Y/Y CPI print = dovish tolerance returns. DXY closing below 100 = market rejecting hawkish read. 30-yr yield sustained above 5.5% = fiscal concerns overtaking carry narrative, complicates USD outlook.

themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs effective Aug 19 — 50% on autos/dairy/alcohol, USMCA compliance no longer a shield
themes.summary: The USMCA/Section 122 binary has resolved and materially escalated for CAD. Section 122 expired July 24 by statutory operation and was replaced by Section 301 (10-12.5% on non-USMCA goods). But the genuinely new and market-moving event is Trump's Jul 20 invocation of Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 — the statute's first use since the 1940s. Three presidential proclamations impose 50% duties on approximately $20B of Canadian goods (autos, dairy, alcohol, electrical machinery, cement) effective August 19, 2026 at 12:01am ET. Critically: USMCA certification provides zero protection on these specific product baskets. Canada has not yet announced retaliation publicly but the precedent from IEEPA/Section 122 cycles suggests symmetric response. USDCAD has already moved on this — the pair rebounded from 1.4002 to test 1.4115+ after the proclamations. The Aug 19 effective date is a hard binary: if Canada capitulates or a deal is struck pre-Aug 19 = sharp CAD relief rally. If tariffs land in full = USDCAD gaps higher, CAD crosses reprice. USMCA review sessions are ongoing but the Section 338 action operates outside the USMCA framework entirely, making the review timeline irrelevant to the Aug 19 risk. Also watch: Trump separately invoked Section 338 on Canadian dairy/auto surtax practices, meaning Canada's retaliation on US-made autos (an existing measure) is the formal legal predicate for the 50% duty.

implications.CAD: STRONG headwind — 50% tariffs on $20B of exports effective Aug 19 with USMCA providing no exemption. Elevated vol both directions into Aug 19 deadline. Wider SLs, smaller sizes on all CAD crosses. USDCAD technically constructive above 1.4002 support.
implications.USD: moderate tailwind via trade-policy narrative and CAD weakness; USDCAD structurally supported.
implications.MXN: elevated secondary exposure — Mexico is separately facing Section 301 successor regime but not the Section 338 escalation. USDMXN moves can telegraph CAD next-session.
implications.EUR: indirect — EU separately under 15% tariff ceiling from Jul 1; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses.
implications.AUD: indirect risk-off if CAD volatility spills into broader commodity bloc; AUDCAD dynamics may shift.

themes.watchLevel: Aug 19 effective date is the primary binary. Pre-Aug 19 Canada capitulation or bilateral deal = sharp CAD relief, retire theme. Tariffs land as scheduled = USDCAD gap higher, extend CAD-bearish bias post-Aug 19. Any Section 338 legal challenge (injunction filed) that pauses collection = uncertainty spike, re-evaluate. Canada retaliatory proclamation = CAD vol surge, pairs move 100+ pips.
